page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtualization instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical dedicated cores with two threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512F, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA, though newer extensions like AMX, VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 are absent. The instance does not bundle any local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results categorize the general processing capabilities of this instance primarily in the lower quartiles. The server registered a single-core Geekbench score of 920.0 and a multi-core score of 3502.0, along with a multi-core stress-ng score of 5855.73. Compression and decompression tasks show modest throughput, with single-threaded gzip achieving 19.04 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 26.37 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 38.27 GB/sec on large un-cached reads and 35.69 GB/sec on writes. In-memory data store evaluations demonstrate 5.79 million Redis SET operations per second, while LLM inference speeds drop significantly with larger model footprints, logging 9.9 prompt tokens per second and 5.08 text generation tokens per second on 7B models.

Given the high memory allocation relative to compute capacity, the server emphasizes capacity-heavy tasks rather than compute-bound performance. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external network storage integration, and the 2 Gbps baseline network caps throughput for data synchronization. The ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is primarily suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, light database operations, internal enterprise tools, and memory-dependent batch ETL jobs where high raw computational throughput is secondary to memory footprint.

The instance includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512F instructions, but lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. Network capabilities feature a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark testing indicates modest CPU performance, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 3502.0 and lower-tier ratings across compute and decompression workloads. Memory bandwidth sustains 38.27 GB/sec for uncached reads and 35.69 GB/sec for writes. The high 8:1 memory-to-core ratio allows cost-efficient memory footprint scaling, making it well suited for in-memory caching systems, background data processing pipelines, and moderate database services that do not require intense sustained compute capacity.
